# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Threads, GL, Xft, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |

feature/batch5-s-m-hacks
"""Copies an xscreensaver hack into the firmware and registers it.

    uv run tools/wire_hack.py <name> <Class> "<copyright text>" \\
        [--notice "<licence column>"] [--xlockmore] [--glx]

Does the mechanical steps of `.claude/skills/port-hack/adding-a-hack.md`
(steps 2 and 3): copies `vendor/xscreensaver-6.16/hacks/<name>.c` to
`firmware/src/hacks/<name>/`, adds the registry entry (last in the button
order), the name to the expected list in `test_hacks.c`, a frame hash of `0`
(skipped until pinned: see "Batches" in that skill), a leak test, and the
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md row. It does not touch `platformio.ini`, write a
wrapper, or fill a shim gap. Read the hack's licence first.

--xlockmore registers with `XLOCKMORE_HACK(name, "Class")`, for a hack built on
xlockmore.h (it has `MI_DISPLAY`); otherwise it expects the hack to define its
own `<name>_hack` through XSCREENSAVER_MODULE.
"""

import argparse
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
UPSTREAM = "vendor/xscreensaver-6.16"


def _insert_before(text: str, marker: str, addition: str) -> str:
    i = text.find(marker)
    if i < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot find `{marker}`")
    return text[:i] + addition + text[i:]


# The After Dark toasters stay last (built only with the disk image), so a new
# hack goes before this guard in each list that has it.
GUARD = "#ifdef HAVE_AFTER_DARK_TOASTERS\n"


def _guard_in(text: str, start: str, end: str) -> int:
    """Index of GUARD between `start` and `end`, or -1."""
    a = text.find(start)
    b = text.find(end, a)
    if a < 0 or b < 0:
        return -1
    return text.find(GUARD, a, b)


def wire(
    root: Path,
    name: str,
    cls: str,
    copyright_text: str,
    notice: str = "jwz permission notice (above)",
    xlockmore: bool = False,
    glx: bool = False,
) -> None:
    src = root / UPSTREAM / "hacks" / ("glx" if glx else "") / f"{name}.c"
    if not src.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(src)
    dst = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / name / f"{name}.c"
    registry = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "registry.c"
    tests = root / "firmware" / "test" / "test_hacks" / "test_hacks.c"
    notices = root / "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"

    reg = registry.read_text()
    if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}_hack\b", reg):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} is already in registry.c")
    if xlockmore:
        decl = f'XLOCKMORE_HACK({name}, "{cls}");\n'
    else:
        decl = f"extern const HackEntry {name}_hack;\n"
    reg = _insert_before(reg, "const HackEntry *const g_hacks[]", decl + "\n")
    g = _guard_in(reg, "g_hacks[] = {", "};")
    if g >= 0:
        reg = reg[:g] + f"    &{name}_hack,\n" + reg[g:]
    else:
        reg, n = re.subn(
            r"    &(\w+)_hack\};", rf"    &\1_hack,\n    &{name}_hack}};", reg, count=1

#!/bin/bash
# Flashes a build that starts on one hack with rotation off, then reads the
# serial log. Needs the board, and Rod's say-so in the session (AGENTS.md:
# never flash without asking, unless he has said it is allowed).
#
#   bash tools/flash_and_capture.sh <hack> <seconds> [extra build flags] [lines]
#
# <hack> is a name from g_hacks[] in any case; extra flags are things like
# "-DFIREWORKX_SCALE=2"; the last `run` lines (default 6) are printed. The full
# log and the flash output go to $OUT_DIR (default: ./flash-capture, which
# should be somewhere git ignores, such as your scratchpad).
set -u
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 2; }
hack=$1 seconds=$2 extra=${3:-} lines=${4:-6}
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
out=${OUT_DIR:-./flash-capture}
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)

source "$repo/tools/env.sh"
cd "$repo/firmware" || exit 1
PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="-DSTART_HACK=\\\"$hack\\\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=0 $extra" \
  NO_COLOR=1 pio run -e stopwatch -t upload > "$out/flash_$hack.txt" 2>&1
pio_status=$?
unset PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS
verified=$(grep -c 'Hash of data verified' "$out/flash_$hack.txt")
echo "flash verified: $verified" "$(grep -E 'Flash:' "$out/flash_$hack.txt")"
grep -E "error:|overflowed" "$out/flash_$hack.txt" | head -3
# A failed flash leaves the old firmware running, and the capture would measure
# that: stop rather than report numbers for the wrong build.
if [ "$pio_status" -ne 0 ] || [ "$verified" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "flash failed (pio exit $pio_status, $verified verified); see $out/flash_$hack.txt" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "note: the board now starts on $hack with rotation off; flash a normal build when done"
"$repo/.venv/bin/python" -I "$repo/tools/serial_capture.py" "$out/$hack.log" "$seconds"
grep -a "^run" "$out/$hack.log" | tail -"$lines" | cut -c1-125

Here's what I found on each. All the numbers for Rocks below are my arithmetic; none are measured.

## Reported problems

- **Triangle (rainbow):** this is my fault. The shim's `make_smooth_colormap` is our own. It always puts three anchors round the whole hue wheel at high saturation and brightness, so it's always a bright rainbow. Upstream picks 2–5 random colours, with random saturation (0–1) and brightness (0.2–1), rejects any pair too close together, and joins them in a loop. That gives the muted, earthy palettes. I'd rewrite ours to follow that behaviour without copying the code. It changes the colours of every hack that uses the smooth scheme, and the pinned hashes with them, so I need your go-ahead.
- **Penrose (screen full, no blank):** this is upstream behaviour, as you suspected. Its restart is a pause counted in frames: `COMPLETION` is 3141 frames, and `CELEBRATE` is 31415. `CELEBRATE` is used when the tiler hits an error or an untileable vertex. At 87 fps that's about 6 minutes, and about 5 minutes at X's usual rate. It also keeps growing into the square's corners, which the round screen hides. I'd shorten both pauses with a build-time patch, as I did for Celtic (the copy stays byte-identical). I'd aim for about 10 s, but that number is my call.
- **Lisa (speed varies):** the hack picks a random line width of 1–8 at each start. Width 1 takes the cheap line path and wider widths go through the polygon stroker. I measured 14.3 fps on one start, so that's one width, not the range. Options: speed up the stroker (shared code), or patch Lisa to cap the width. Capping is simplest, but it changes the look.

## Rocks and the shim

I need to correct my earlier note. The shim already has 1-bit bitmaps and `XCopyPlane` from them to the window. What it lacks is *drawing into* a bitmap: `XFillRectangle` and `XFillPolygon` do nothing there. Rocks fills a rock silhouette into about 400 bitmaps at start-up, then stamps them each frame. So the stamps are blank and only the tiny far dots, drawn as plain rectangles, show.

Adding bitmap fills is a real gap fill. I'd need to check it doesn't move any pinned hack (Goop creates a 1-bit pixmap), and the full suite would tell me. My estimates:

- **PSRAM:** about 2.7 MB of bitmaps, which fits beside the 7 MB free.
- **Start-up:** about 10 M pixel writes to fill the bitmaps, unless I fill them in spans with bit operations.
- **Frame rate:** the per-pixel `XCopyPlane` loop could limit it. I'd measure it before promising anything.

## DecayScreen image

The shim already has a blob format (`565M` in `ximage-loader.h`) and `tools/make_logo_blob.py`, which uses Pillow. So any PNG or JPEG is fine, and I'll convert it. Square, at least 466 px, with the subject centred (the screen is round) is ideal. Size matters because the image lives in flash. A full 466×466 blob is 434 KB, and I'd guess about 0.7 MB is left in the 3 MB partition, which I haven't checked. I'd store 320×320 (200 KB) and scale up, or 233×233 (108 KB) if space is tight. I'd wire it into `load_image_async_simple`, so any hack that wants a picture gets it. Rotzoomer and Twang are probably candidates, but I haven't checked.

## Questions for you

1. Shall I go ahead with the Triangle colours, the Penrose pause patch and the Rocks bitmap fills? The first and last change shared shim code.
2. For Lisa, should I cap the line width, or look at speeding up the stroker?
3. Which image, and is a 320 px stored size fine?

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: with XS_LOGO=<image> set, writes a logo header
for Maze from that image; without it, removes any header left by an earlier
build so the committed logo is used.

maze_patched.c includes "images/gen/logo-50_png.h" from its own directory
first, so the generated copy wins without touching the include path. Relative
paths are taken from the repository root. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in
PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = (
    Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR"))  # noqa: F821
    / "generated"
    / "images"
    / "gen"
    / "logo-50_png.h"
)
LOGO_SIZE = 50

logo = os.environ.get("XS_LOGO")
if not logo:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    image = Path(logo)
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_LOGO={logo}: no such file ({image})")
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("XS_LOGO needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "logo_50_png",
            "--size",
            str(LOGO_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Maze logo: {image}")

def build_blob(width: int, height: int, rgba: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not (0 < width <= 0xFFFF and 0 < height <= 0xFFFF):
        raise ValueError(f"size {width}x{height} does not fit the blob header")
    if len(rgba) != width * height * 4:
        raise ValueError(f"expected {width * height * 4} RGBA bytes, got {len(rgba)}")

    pixels = bytearray()
    mask = bytearray()
    stride = (width + 7) // 8
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray(stride)
        for x in range(width):
            r, g, b, a = rgba[(y * width + x) * 4 :][:4]
            opaque = a >= OPAQUE_ALPHA
            pixels += (rgb565(r, g, b) if opaque else 0).to_bytes(2, "little")
            if opaque:
                row[x // 8] |= 0x80 >> (x % 8)
        mask += row
    header = b"565M" + width.to_bytes(2, "little") + height.to_bytes(2, "little")
    return bytes(header + pixels + mask)


def c_header(name: str, blob: bytes, source: str) -> str:
    guard = f"XSHIM_{name.upper()}_H"
    lines = []
    for i in range(0, len(blob), 12):
        lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blob[i : i + 12]) + ",")
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    return (
        f"/* Generated by tools/make_logo_blob.py from {source}; do not edit.\n"
        " * Despite the name (maze.c asks for a PNG), this is the raw blob\n"
        " * described in ximage-loader.h. */\n"
        f"#ifndef {guard}\n"
        f"#define {guard}\n"
        f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{\n"
        f"{body}\n"
        "};\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    from PIL import Image

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("image")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C array name")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--size",
        type=int,
        help="shrink to fit this many pixels square, keeping the aspect ratio "
        "(never enlarges)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    image = Image.open(args.image).convert("RGBA")
    if args.size:
        image.thumbnail((args.size, args.size), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    blob = build_blob(image.width, image.height, image.tobytes())

    # Left alone when unchanged, so an unchanged logo does not rebuild.
    output = Path(args.output)
    text = c_header(args.name, blob, Path(args.image).name)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not output.exists() or output.read_text() != text:
        output.write_text(text)
    print(f"{args.output}: {image.width}x{image.height}, {len(blob)} bytes")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Shrink maze.c's fixed-size arrays so it fits in the ESP32-S3's memory.

maze.c keeps its maze and three move lists in one `struct state` sized by
`MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X/Y` (1000 each), about 20 MB. The board has 8 MB of PSRAM. On
a 466 px screen with 7 px cells (the smallest the hack picks) a maze is 66
cells across, so 80 leaves room and the struct drops to about 130 KB.

The copied maze.c stays byte-identical to upstream. The firmware build writes
a patched copy with `firmware/patch_maze.py` and compiles that instead.
"""

import re

MAZE_LIMIT = 80
UPSTREAM_LIMIT = 1000


def patch_maze(source: str, limit: int) -> str:
    for axis in ("X", "Y"):
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"^#define[ \t]+MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis}[ \t]+{UPSTREAM_LIMIT}[ \t]*$",
            re.MULTILINE,
        )
        source, count = pattern.subn(f"#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis} {limit}", source)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"expected one `#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis} {UPSTREAM_LIMIT}`, "
                f"found {count}; has upstream maze.c changed?"
            )
    return source

"""Shorten penrose.c's two pauses so a finished or failed tiling restarts soon.

penrose.c counts its pauses in frames, tuned for a fast X server:
`COMPLETION` (3141) after the tiles fill the screen and `CELEBRATE` (31415)
after an error it expects to recover from, which is about six minutes at the
board's 87 frames a second with the screen full and nothing moving. Both
become `PAUSE_FRAMES`, about ten seconds.

The copied penrose.c stays byte-identical to upstream. The firmware build
writes a patched copy with `firmware/patch_penrose.py` and compiles that.
"""

import re

PAUSE_FRAMES = 900
UPSTREAM = {"CELEBRATE": 31415, "COMPLETION": 3141}


def shorten_pauses(source: str, frames: int) -> str:
    for name, value in UPSTREAM.items():
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"^#define[ \t]+{name}[ \t]+{value}\b[^\n]*$", re.MULTILINE
        )
        source, count = pattern.subn(f"#define {name} {frames}", source)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"expected one `#define {name} {value}`, found {count}; "
                "has upstream penrose.c changed?"
            )
    return source

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The default is firmware/assets/grab-image.jpg, scaled to fit 320 pixels (about
217 KB of flash). XS_GRAB_IMAGE=<image> uses another (relative paths are taken
from the repository root) and XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none builds without one, so the
hacks that want a picture load nothing. A header from an earlier build is
removed in that case. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 320

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
if choice == "none":
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project / "assets" / "grab-image.jpg"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice}: no such file ({image})")
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The picture is vendor/grab-image.png when that exists, or the file named by
XS_GRAB_IMAGE (relative paths are taken from the repository root). It is
scaled to fit 466 pixels (a 640 by 480 screenshot becomes 466 by 350, about
340 KB of flash). Without either, or with XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none, nothing is
generated and a hack that wants a picture loads nothing. vendor/ is
git-ignored, so a picture someone else owns (the Windows 95 screenshot) stays
out of the repository. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in PlatformIO's
Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 466

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
image = None
if choice != "none":
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project.parent / "vendor" / "grab-image.png"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        if choice:
            sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice}: no such file ({image})")
        image = None

if image is None:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")
